problem: The gold-aware Visible-Pivot oracle passed exactly 4/7, but one rescue used frontmatter formatting metadata and the oracle enumerated up to 64 gold-overlap terms across every frozen query. It does not show that a runtime harness can choose a semantic pivot under a realistic search budget.
simplest_baseline: Choose no pivot and reuse the frozen queries; full-document BM25 top-20 remains 0/7.
hypothesis: After removing wrappers and YAML frontmatter, the two rarest provenance-bound capitalized body terms per case, selected without gold documents or answers, retain gold-document top-20 retrieval on at least two of the four oracle-rescued cases and at least two of seven cases overall.
anti_claim: This selector is calibrated on outcome-selected failures with frozen model parameters. Any hit is a harness retrieval-selection result, not a model-capability improvement or unseen effectiveness result.

framework_comparisons.current_gap: A deterministic two-pivot slate tests whether another research branch has a viable evidence-derived target before paying for a new isolated context.
The selector keeps the backend fixed and adds a provenance-preserving transition from compressed visible evidence to one bounded follow-up query.
The fixed two-query slate is a cheaper falsification than adding crawler breadth after an oracle that still contained a metadata artifact.
This is a fixed one-edge selector with explicit source provenance; graph expansion remains unjustified unless the edge survives without gold labels.

next_action: Freeze this rarity-first capitalized-token selector: it selected two body candidates for every case with zero gold/answer/frontmatter leakage, but recovered 0/7 and retained 0/4 oracle rescues. Do not increase slate size or reorder the same candidates on these observed cases. Before another end-to-end run, open a separately registered candidate-representation question, such as typed entity/relation linking from visible evidence, and require it to beat this fixed 0/7 selector without adding Agent roles or changing the retriever simultaneously.
claim_boundary: This is a no-gold selector calibration on already observed failures. Only a later fixed-budget unseen development run can support an effectiveness claim.
